newsitem.title: USA: Pioneer Hi-Bred shares rise on DuPont deal.
newsitem.headline: Pioneer Hi-Bred shares rise on DuPont deal.

text.p: Shares of agriculture company Pioneer Hi-Bred International Inc rose 16-4/16 to 92-13/16 after DuPont Co said it would buy 20 percent of Pioneer for $104 a share.
Pioneer said it will hold a Dutch auction tender offer to buy from the public an equivalent amount of shares.
Pioneer and DuPont also agreed to a research alliance, formed a joint venture company, and signed a 16-year standstill and corporate governance agreement.
Prudential Securities analyst John McMillin said the deal would enable Pioneer, which had been rumored to be a possible takeover target, to remain an independent company.

"There was some concern that they (Pioneer) might get taken over," McMillin said. "DuPont will own 20 percent of the stock and insiders control at least that amount. In effect, the voting control of Pioneer will be held by insiders."
McMillin added that the deal with DuPont couples Pioneer, which has a broad portfolio of seed germ plasm, with a strong partner.
"It positions (Pioneer) better in this new age of biotechnology in the sense that they're aligned now with a research giant," McMillin said.
